guidance: Media card planning only: it turns a card size and a camera bitrate into recording time, card fill, copy storage and offload time. It is not an encoder bitrate or target-size planner, and not a recorder retention calculator.
method: Recording time per card = card size in GB x 8000 / bitrate in Mbps: a GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes and a megabit is 1,000,000 bits, so the constant folds the eight bits in a byte and the two decimal prefixes together. Space per hour = bitrate x 0.45 GB of decimal gigabytes, and per minute that value divided by 60. The cards a shoot needs is the planned minutes divided by the minutes one card holds, rounded up to a whole card. Storage for every copy = planned minutes x space per minute x the number of copies chosen. Offload read time = card size in GB x 1000 / the reader's rated MB/s, one read pass per card whatever the number of copies. The same capacity is also reported in GiB (2^30 bytes) because operating systems often show a card as smaller than its label. Card size runs from 1 to 8192 GB with up to one decimal, bitrate from 1 to 20000 Mbps, cards from 1 to 99, footage from 1 to 60000 minutes and reader speed from 1 to 20000 MB/s; every field is validated and each error names the field and its range. No container, file-system, clip or proxy overhead is counted, the bitrate is held constant for the whole shoot, audio is assumed to sit inside the bitrate entered, and the reader's rated speed is taken at face value, so real recording times are a few percent shorter and real offloads slower. It plans media only: it reads no card, lists no camera's approved media, computes no encoder target size and no recorder retention, keeps no record, and runs entirely in the browser with no uploads, accounts or network access.
